newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta edges up on dollar, renewed euro optimism.
newsitem.headline: Peseta edges up on dollar, renewed euro optimism.

text.p: The peseta gained slightly against the mark early on Thursday, buttressed by a rise in the dollar and underpinned by views the single currency would start on time and that Spain would be in the launch.
"It seems that everything is going well, at least in Spain, and I believe that despite the nervousness about the euro, at the end of the day, monetary union will start on time," a dealer said.
At 0820 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.53/58 per mark versus 84.54/57 at the outset of trade and 84.59/61 late on Wednesday.
In addition, the dollar was benefitting from expectations that next week the Amsterdam summit would ratify the stability pact, which would clear the route to Maastricht.
